chunks: We were told by my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they both said: We were told by Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muqil ibn Sulayman, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

When Musa (peace be upon him) climbed the mountain and silently called to his Lord, Exalted and Glorious is He, he said: O my Lord, show me Your treasures. He said: O Musa, My treasures is only that when I want something, I say to it: «Be» and it is.
ai.seo_question: What did Allah reveal as His greatest treasure to Prophet Musa?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that the 'treasures' of Allah are not material stores but the divine attribute of absolute creative power, encapsulated in the command 'Kun' (Be). This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on God's direct, effortless will (*Irada*) as the sole mechanism of creation, distinguishing it from created means or instruments. The dialogue underscores the transcendence of Allah, who requires no preparation or accumulation to manifest His will.

en.basel-kadem: 63. We were told by my father, and Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they both said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Hasan bin Mahbub, from Muqatil bin Sulayman, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (as) say: “

When Musa (as) climbed the mountain and silently called to his Lord, Exalted and Glorious is He, he said: O my Lord, show me Your treasures. He said: O Musa, My treasures is only that when I want something, I say to it: «Be» and it is.”
